title: How are orthologs calculated?
taxa_covered: More than 1,200 species in currently covered eukaryotic clades
data_type: RefSeq annotations; protein similarity; exon, UTR and flanking nucleotide similarity; local microsynteny
inference_method: All-to-all protein comparison followed by nucleotide and +/-10-gene-neighborhood evaluation; one-to-one pairs are tracked and anchor groups expanded transitively
model: Thresholded high-precision one-to-one locus assignment with possible RefSeq curator review
topology_claim: None; this method supplies ortholog candidates and does not infer a phylogeny
conflicts: NCBI ortholog calls support reference sampling but do not constrain the BRCA1 gene-tree topology
limitations: Strict one-to-one calls favor precision over recall; coverage is limited to annotated clades and transitive anchors

title: Retrieve ortholog data and metadata
taxa_covered: Human BRCA1 GeneID 672 and its available NCBI ortholog set
data_type: Gene metadata plus protein and RNA FASTA in an NCBI Datasets gene package
inference_method: `datasets download gene gene-id 672 --ortholog all`; metadata can be summarized with `dataformat`
topology_claim: None; the command retrieves records and does not establish a tree
conflicts: Retrieved records are candidates for QC, not species-tree expectations or BRCA1 topology constraints
limitations: A dynamic database result depends on the retrieval date and current RefSeq annotations

title: NCBI Orthologs: Public Resource and Scalable Method for Computing High-Precision Orthologs Across Eukaryotic Genomes
data_type: Protein sequences; exonic nucleotide sequences with 2-kb flanks; microsynteny
inference_method: Competing locus pairs are scored across protein, nucleotide and neighborhood evidence to call high-confidence one-to-one orthologs
model: Multi-threshold decision process anchored to selected reference genomes
topology_claim: None; ortholog-set membership is not a gene-tree or species-tree result
conflicts: Orthology evidence supports inclusion, but it must not be used as a topological constraint on BRCA1
limitations: High precision intentionally sacrifices recall and can omit ambiguous duplicates

title: BRCA1 - Breast cancer type 1 susceptibility protein - Homo sapiens (P38398)
taxa_covered: Homo sapiens canonical BRCA1 isoform 1, 1,863 aa
data_type: Curated protein sequence and cross-database domain annotations
inference_method: Manual UniProt curation integrated with PROSITE, Pfam, SMART, InterPro and other signatures
model: Canonical sequence has RING-type zinc finger 24-65, BRCT 1 at 1642-1736 and BRCT 2 at 1756-1855
topology_claim: One N-terminal RING and two C-terminal BRCT domains are expected in the human query
conflicts: This is sequence-architecture evidence, not a species-tree expectation or topology constraint
limitations: Coordinates are for human canonical P38398-1; ortholog boundaries and central low-complexity regions may differ

title: Rapid evolution of BRCA1 and BRCA2 in humans and other primates
taxa_covered: 23 simian primates, including Homo sapiens and Pan troglodytes
data_type: Full-length BRCA1 coding sequences plus population polymorphism data
inference_method: Branch and site dN/dS analyses in PAML
model: Free-ratio, one-ratio, two-ratio and site-selection models
topology_claim: Repeated amino-acid positive selection was detected in primate BRCA1, with emphasis on the human-chimpanzee-bonobo lineage
conflicts: BRCA1 can carry locus-specific selective signal; its gene tree must not be forced to a primate species tree
limitations: Primate-only selection analysis; it does not validate orthology or topology across the full amniote sample

title: Genome of the marsupial Monodelphis domestica reveals innovation in non-coding sequences
taxa_covered: Monodelphis domestica with eutherian genome comparisons
data_type: Whole-genome shotgun assembly, gene annotation and multi-species comparative genomics
inference_method: Comparative alignment and annotation of the first metatherian reference genome
topology_claim: Metatheria, represented by Monodelphis, is the closest sampled outgroup to Eutheria (placental mammals)
conflicts: Species-tree expectation only; it is not a topological constraint on the BRCA1 gene tree
limitations: The paper is a genome analysis rather than a dedicated modern mammal species-tree inference

title: A genomic timescale for placental mammal evolution
taxa_covered: 241 placental mammals spanning every order, including the placental lineages represented in this BRCA1 example
data_type: Whole-genome alignments; nearly neutral noncoding sites; structural variants
inference_method: Coalescent SVDquartets, concatenated maximum likelihood, locus-tree and rare-genomic-change analyses
model: Coalescent and concatenation frameworks with sensitivity analyses
topology_claim: Supports the major placental clades Afrotheria, Xenarthra, Euarchontoglires and Laurasiatheria; selected primates, Glires and laurasiatherians should cluster within those species clades
conflicts: Species-tree expectation only; it is not a topological constraint on the BRCA1 gene tree
limitations: Monodelphis is outside the placental scope; chromosome-specific discordance and rapid radiations remain relevant

title: The tuatara genome reveals ancient features of amniote evolution
taxa_covered: 27 tetrapods and 245 single-copy orthologues; exact Anolis carolinensis plus representative mammals, squamates, turtles, crocodilians and birds
data_type: Fourfold-degenerate whole-genome sites and single-copy orthologue clusters
inference_method: RAxML maximum likelihood plus ASTRAL gene-tree summary; penalized-likelihood and Bayesian dating
model: GTR+G for orthologue gene trees; genome-scale nucleotide models
topology_claim: Amniotes split into mammalian Synapsida and reptile-plus-bird Sauropsida; Lepidosauria is monophyletic
conflicts: Species-tree expectation only; it is not a topological constraint on the BRCA1 gene tree
limitations: Pseudonaja textilis was not the sampled snake; the lepidosaur statement is a broader-clade comparison

title: Three crocodilian genomes reveal ancestral patterns of evolution among archosaurs
taxa_covered: Crocodylus porosus, painted turtle and representative crocodilian, bird, turtle, lepidosaur, mammal and amphibian genomes
data_type: 965 UCE-anchored loci, 337 single-copy genes and a 23-reptile whole-genome alignment
inference_method: Partitioned RAxML maximum likelihood with 500 bootstraps plus concordant gene and genome analyses
topology_claim: Crocodilians are sister to birds (Archosauria), and turtles are sister to living archosaurs
conflicts: Species-tree expectation only; it is not a topological constraint on the BRCA1 gene tree
limitations: Very slow crocodilian and turtle rates are genome-wide context; the study does not analyze BRCA1 specifically

title: Complexity of avian evolution revealed by family-level genomes
taxa_covered: 363 bird species from 218 families, covering Galliformes and Passeriformes represented by Gallus and Taeniopygia in this example
data_type: 63,430 one-kilobase intergenic loci from whole-genome alignments
inference_method: IQ-TREE locus trees with weak branches collapsed; ASTRAL-MP species tree; partitioned RAxML-NG comparison
model: Per-locus substitution models and multispecies-coalescent summary
topology_claim: Galliformes and Passeriformes occupy distinct neognath branches but remain within a monophyletic avian lineage
conflicts: Species-tree expectation only; it is not a topological constraint on the BRCA1 gene tree
limitations: Deep avian nodes show incomplete lineage sorting, compositional effects and alternative genomic signals

title: Phylogenomics Reveals Ancient Gene Tree Discordance in the Amphibian Tree of Life
taxa_covered: 286 amphibian species across 220 loci, including Rhinatrema bivittatum and broad anuran sampling relevant to Xenopus
inference_method: Concatenated and coalescent species-tree analyses, locus-by-locus topology tests and MCMCTree dating
model: Partitioned sequence models and multispecies-coalescent comparisons
topology_claim: Supports Amphibia and Batrachia; the caecilian Rhinatrema lies outside frog-plus-salamander Batrachia, so the two amphibian outgroups span a deep split
conflicts: Species-tree expectation only; it is not a topological constraint on the BRCA1 gene tree; the paper explicitly documents gene-tree discordance
limitations: Only two amphibian tips are retained here, so the BRCA1 example cannot represent the full deep-amphibian topology
